routes.name: Schengen Uniform Visa (short stay)
routes.summary: Short visit visa valid for up to 90 days in any 180-day period, for tourism, business, family visits, study and more. Romania is in the Schengen area, so check the official visa-free list for your passport first.

other: Visa-free list by nationality not read from an official page. Check the EU list and the Romanian MFA site.
Romania's full Schengen status since 2025 not confirmed on a page I could open.

routes.processing: Apply at least 2 weeks and no more than 3 months before travel. Fees not confirmed.
steps: Book and attend the in-person visit at a Romanian mission or consulate

routes.name: Visa with Limited Territorial Validity
routes.summary: Issued only in exceptional cases, such as humanitarian reasons or national interest. Valid in one or some Schengen states, not all.

stay.note: Validity set by the issuing mission.

routes.name: Airport Transit Visa (type A)
routes.summary: Lets you pass through the international transit area of a Romanian airport without entering the country. You cannot leave the transit area, even overnight. Multiple-entry versions are valid up to six months. Romania no longer issues type B transit visas.

other: Which nationalities need an airport transit visa was not confirmed.

routes.name: Long-Stay Visa for Employment (D/AM)
routes.summary: National type D visa for work. The employer applies on the WorkinRomania platform for skilled workers, and a placement agency or authorized employer applies for permanent, seasonal and cross-border workers. A work permit from IGI is usually needed first.

other: Some groups are exempt from the work permit, such as certain academic or artistic staff.
Seasonal visas last the contract plus 5 days, up to 90 days.

stay.note: The visa is valid 90 days. Then you apply for a residence permit at IGI at least 30 days before it expires.

routes.processing: Visa decisions within 30 days of filing. Work permit decisions take up to 20 days (up to 60 for exempt groups).

routes.name: Long-Stay Visa for Secondment and Intra-Corporate Transfer (D/DT)
routes.summary: For qualified staff posted from an EU, EEA or Swiss employer, intra-corporate transferees, and some academic or scientific roles. A work permit from IGI is required.

other: ICT specialists need at least 3 years of relevant experience.
EU-posted staff: 12 months, extendable to 18 within 36 months.

routes.processing: About 10 days after the work permit, up to 30 for exempt categories.

routes.name: Long-Stay Visa for Business, Liberal Professions and Commercial Activity (D/AE, D/AP, D/AC)
routes.summary: For regulated economic activity, liberal professions, and shareholders or associates who manage a Romanian company.

other: Exact financial and company requirements not read.

routes.name: Long-Stay Visa for Company Administrator or Branch Manager (D/AS)
routes.summary: For non-shareholder administrators of a Romanian company that registered a contribution or technology transfer of at least EUR 50,000. Also for managers of a foreign company's Romanian branch with no Romanian shareholders or administrators.

other: Company must have registered at least EUR 50,000 contribution or technology transfer.
Branch managers need funds at least equal to the guaranteed minimum gross national salary.

routes.name: Digital Nomad Long-Stay Visa (D/AS)
routes.summary: For remote workers earning income from outside Romania. You need means of subsistence of at least three times the average gross monthly salary for each of the previous six months.

other: Income must come from outside Romania.
Three times the average gross monthly salary in each of the last 6 months. The euro amount was not on the page.

stay.note: D visa is valid 90 days, then a residence permit through IGI.

routes.name: Long-Stay Visa for Studies (D/SD)
routes.summary: For full-time students at accredited institutions (bachelor's, master's, PhD, postdoc), pupils aged 13 to 19, and trainees with or pursuing a higher education degree.

other: Accepted by an accredited or temporarily authorized institution.

routes.name: Long-Stay Visa for Family Reunification (D/VF)
routes.summary: For spouses and minor children of residents (permit valid at least 1 year, EU Blue Card, ICT permit), and for spouses, partners with a child, children and parents of Romanian citizens.

routes.name: Other Long-Stay Visas (volunteer, au pair, medical, religious, research, sports)
routes.summary: Type D visas exist for volunteers (14+), au pairs (18 to 30, up to 25 hours a week), long-term medical treatment, recognized religious activity, scientific research, professional sports and unpaid training.

other: Each category has its own paperwork. Check eViza.

routes.name: Working Holiday Visa (D/VM)
routes.summary: Governed by bilateral treaties. The official page says no such treaty is currently in place, so this route is not open.

other: No working holiday agreements in force.

routes.name: Temporary Residence Permit (extension of stay)
routes.summary: After a type D visa you apply for a residence permit at an IGI territorial office at least 30 days before the visa expires. Applications can be started on the IGI online portal.

other: Permit lengths, fees and documents not confirmed.

steps: Apply at IGI at least 30 days before the visa ends
Use the IGI portal to upload documents first

routes.name: Permanent / Long-Term Residence
routes.summary: Permanent residence is required before applying for citizenship. Years needed and conditions were not confirmed from an official page.

other: Years and requirements not read. Check IGI.

routes.name: Citizenship by Naturalization (Article 8)
routes.summary: You need 8 years of legal residence, or 5 years from the date of marriage to a Romanian citizen, plus permanent residence. You must read and write Romanian and know the Constitution, anthem, and basics of Romanian history, geography and culture.

other: Clean criminal record from Romania and countries lived in.
Proof of housing and lawful income for last 3 years where applicable.
Fees and the format of the knowledge test not listed on the page.
Dual citizenship not addressed on the page.

citizenship.note: 5 years if married to a Romanian citizen, counted from the marriage date.

routes.name: Citizenship by Descent or Reacquisition
routes.summary: Romania has routes for former citizens and descendants to reacquire citizenship. The official page was blocked, so the generations allowed and the conditions are not confirmed.

other: Generation limits and documents not confirmed. Check cetatenie.just.ro.

routes.name: EU/EEA/Swiss Free Movement
routes.summary: EU, EEA and Swiss citizens can live and work in Romania under EU free movement rules. Registration rules not read from an official page.

other: Registration details not confirmed.
